# smartbanner-tsx

> smartbanner-tsx is a Smart App Banner component for React 18 and 19. It shows a native-looking "open in the App Store / Google Play" banner on mobile websites to promote iOS and Android apps. It has zero runtime dependencies (~2.5 KB gzipped), is SSR-safe (Next.js App Router, Remix), written in TypeScript, and can be themed with CSS variables or replaced with your own markup through the `useSmartBanner()` hook.

Key facts:

- Install: `npm install smartbanner-tsx`. Peer dependencies: `react` and `react-dom` 18 or 19.
- Usage: `import { SmartBanner } from "smartbanner-tsx"; import "smartbanner-tsx/style.css";` then render `<SmartBanner title="My App" author="My Company" />`.
- App IDs come from `<meta name="apple-itunes-app" content="app-id=...">` and `<meta name="google-play-app" content="app-id=...">`, or from the `appId={{ ios, android }}` prop. Without an app ID the banner is not shown.
- The banner shows on Android and on iOS browsers without Apple's native banner (Chrome, Firefox, in-app browsers). It is skipped in iOS Safari (use `ignoreIosVersion` to show it there), on desktop (use `force="ios"` or `force="android"` to preview), and in installed PWAs.
- After close it is hidden for `daysHidden` days (default 15, cookie `smartbanner-closed`); after the button click for `daysReminder` days (default 90, cookie `smartbanner-installed`). `resetSmartBanner()` clears both.
- Theming: CSS variables such as `--smartbanner-bg`, `--smartbanner-button-bg`, `--smartbanner-button-radius`, `--smartbanner-height`, set on `:root`, `.smartbanner-ios`, `.smartbanner-android` or via the `style` prop.
- Headless: `useSmartBanner(options)` returns `{ visible, platform, appId, link, icon, description, t, close, install }`.
- v2 keeps the v1 props, meta tags, class names and markup. To keep the v1 look import `smartbanner-tsx/classic.css`.
- License: MIT.
